DIRECTION A — Full-bleed cycle

One poster fills the hero. Every 4–5s the next one crossfades in. The wordmark IS the poster (each poster already renders Drip), so no overlay text fights the background.

+ Cinematic, always brand-forward, calm.
– No room for a spoken headline beyond what the poster says.

DIRECTION B — Editorial split

Left 55% is quiet brand — giant italic Drip wordmark, one-line tagline, red "Pull Up" CTA. Right 45% is a poster window that slot-cycles.

+ Room for real copy and a clear CTA above the fold.
– Less full-bleed / cinematic; feels more magazine-cover than immersive.

DIRECTION C — Poster stack

One dominant poster centered, two flanks peeking at 30–40% opacity behind. The center rotates through the deck; flanks come from and return to the wings.

+ Depth, museum-wall feel, teases variety without splitting the frame.
– Complex motion, careful timing needed to not feel cluttered.

DIRECTION D — Triple mosaic

Hero is three vertical bands, each showing a different poster ken-burning independently. A single italic Drip wordmark composites on top of all three, dead-center.

+ Loudest, most "three vibes at once" — great for a taste-forward brand.
– Busiest. Wordmark needs the blurred plate behind it to stay readable across three different backgrounds.

DRIP — HERO DIRECTIONS

Dropping the .mov entirely (baked-in letterboxing was killing it) and driving the hero off the 13 brand posters instead. Below are four ways to compose them. Each artboard is desktop-scale (1440×900). Pick one and I'll build it into the site with the tilt + spotlight-reveal effects layered on top.
